question: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg increases diuresis because:

options.opb: Decreases the peritubular reabsorption of water.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg -> increases hydrostatic pressure in the glomerulus -> enhances glomerular filtration rate -> increases urine production -> increases diuresis -> 80%
CHAIN: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg -> leads to constriction of the efferent arteriole -> increases glomerular filtration rate -> promotes diuresis -> 75%

CHAIN: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg -> causes dilation of the afferent arteriole -> increases glomerular perfusion pressure -> enhances glomerular filtration rate -> promotes diuresis -> 70%
enhanced_information: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg increases diuresis because it enhances glomerular filtration rate, leading to increased urine production. This is primarily due to the increase in hydrostatic pressure in the glomerulus, promoting filtration. The efferent arteriole contraction and afferent arteriole dilation may play a role in regulating glomerular perfusion pressure, but the main mechanism is the increase in glomerular filtration rate.
analysis: An increase in blood pressure between 80 and 150 mmHg leads to increased diuresis primarily by enhancing the glomerular filtration rate due to increased hydrostatic pressure in the glomerulus. The efferent arteriole contraction and afferent arteriole dilation may modulate glomerular perfusion pressure but are not the main mechanisms for diuresis.
